entries.description: Aboriginal Australians arrived on the continent at least 60
entries.subject: Aboriginal Australians

spans.text:
### Background

Aboriginal Australians arrived on the continent at least 60,000 years ago and developed complex hunter-gatherer societies and oral histories.

entries.description: Abel TASMAN were the first Europeans to land in Australia in 1606
entries.subject: Abel TASMAN
entries.object: the first Europeans to land in Australia in 1606

spans.text: Dutch navigators led by Abel TASMAN were the first Europeans to land in Australia in 1606, and they mapped the western and northern coasts.

entries.task_id: james cook|sailed|to the east coast of australia
entries.description: James COOK sailed to the east coast of Australia
entries.subject: James COOK
entries.object: to the east coast of Australia

spans.text: In 1770, Englishman James COOK sailed to the east coast of Australia, named it New South Wales, and claimed it for Great Britain.

entries.task_id: great britain|established|new south wales and then tasmania as penal colonies
entries.description: Great Britain established New South Wales and then Tasmania as penal colonies
entries.subject: Great Britain
entries.object: New South Wales and then Tasmania as penal colonies

spans.text: In 1788 and 1825 respectively, Great Britain established New South Wales and then Tasmania as penal colonies.
Great Britain and Ireland sent more than 150,000 convicts to Australia before ending the practice in 1868.

entries.task_id: as europeans|began|settling areas away from the coasts
entries.description: As Europeans began settling areas away from the coasts
entries.subject: As Europeans
entries.object: settling areas away from the coasts

spans.text: As Europeans began settling areas away from the coasts, they came into more direct contact with Aboriginal Australians.

entries.task_id: additional colonies|were|established in australia in the mid-1800s: western australia (1829)
entries.description: additional colonies were established in Australia in the mid-1800s: Western Australia (1829)
entries.subject: additional colonies
entries.object: established in Australia in the mid-1800s: Western Australia (1829)

spans.text:
These issues, along with disease and a policy in the 1900s that forcefully removed Aboriginal children from their parents, reduced the Aboriginal Australian population from more than 700,000 pre-European contact to a low of 74,000 in 1933.

Four additional colonies were established in Australia in the mid-1800s: Western Australia (1829), South Australia (1836), Victoria (1851), and Queensland (1859).

entries.description: the colonies were all gradually granted self-government
entries.subject: the colonies

spans.text: In the second half of the 1800s, the colonies were all gradually granted self-government, and in 1901, they federated and became the Commonwealth of Australia.
Australia’s post-war economy boomed and by the 1970s, racial policies that prevented most non-Whites from immigrating to Australia were removed, greatly increasing Asian immigration to the country.

entries.description: Australia has become an internationally competitive
entries.subject: Australia

spans.text: In recent decades, Australia has become an internationally competitive, advanced market economy due in large part to economic reforms adopted in the 1980s and its proximity to East and Southeast Asia.
